short: An American strategic reconnaissance aircraft capable of flying at Mach 3+ and the fastest air-breathing manned aircraft ever built.
full:
Introduced in 1966, the Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird was developed as a highly classified strategic reconnaissance platform for the United States Air Force. Designed to operate at extreme altitudes and speeds exceeding Mach 3, it could survey vast swaths of hostile territory while remaining largely invulnerable to interception. Rather than evading surface-to-air missiles with maneuvers, its standard defensive tactic was simply to accelerate and outfly them.

The Blackbird's titanium airframe was engineered to withstand the intense friction heat generated by sustained supersonic flight. Operating through the height of the Cold War, it provided invaluable intelligence without a single airframe ever being lost to enemy fire. High operating costs and the advent of advanced reconnaissance satellites led to its final retirement in 1999.
